important_decisions.rationale: In apply_table_apa7_and_bidi and post_process_openxml within compile_gold_standard_chapter4.py, the script injected <w:bidiVisual w:val='1'/> instead of an empty <w:bidiVisual/>. The developer assumed that because boolean properties like <w:bidi w:val='1'/> use w:val, table bidiVisual also requires w:val='1'. In ISO/IEC 29500-1 §17.4.2, bidiVisual is an OnOffOnlyType element where presence indicates true without attributes. Microsoft Word's desktop GUI Table Properties dialog specifically checks for the empty element <w:bidiVisual/> and fails to map <w:bidiVisual w:val='1'/> to its Right-to-left radio button, displaying 'Left-to-right' instead.

alternatives_considered.reason: Microsoft Word's Table Properties dialog parser recognizes <w:bidiVisual/> as RTL but fails on unexpected w:val attribute.
Omitting bidiVisual makes table column order physically Left-to-Right.

important_decisions.rationale: In compile_gold_standard_chapter4.py lines 727-742, sectPr was moved to the end of the body and modified via doc.sections margin properties, which left <w:docGrid w:linePitch='360'/> at the end of sectPr without inserting <w:bidi/>. When scripts attempted to add bidi via sectPr.append(bidi), <w:bidi/> was positioned AFTER <w:docGrid/>. Under ISO/IEC 29500-1 §17.6.17 (CT_SectPr), <w:bidi/> MUST precede <w:docGrid/>. When Microsoft Word encounters <w:bidi/> after <w:docGrid/>, its graceful degradation error recovery ignores the out-of-order element, causing section-level LTR fallback that forces tables inside the section to default to LTR in GUI dialogs.

alternatives_considered.reason: Schema order mandates: ... -> textDirection -> bidi -> rtlGutter -> docGrid -> printerSettings.
Placing bidi after docGrid triggers OpenXML deserialization error recovery in Microsoft Word.

important_decisions.rationale: In compile_gold_standard_chapter4.py lines 571-676 (post_process_docx_zip), the compiler exclusively unzipped and edited word/document.xml, leaving word/settings.xml untouched. In OpenXML §17.15.1, word/settings.xml must declare <w:themeFontLang w:bidi='fa-IR'/> and modern compatibilityMode=15 to configure Word's BiDi engine for Persian. Without document-level w:bidi='fa-IR', Microsoft Word defaults its internal locale to Western/LTR, causing table GUI dialogs to open in Left-to-Right mode.

alternatives_considered.reason: Instructs Word application and GUI dialogs that the active complex-script locale is Persian.
Run-level <w:lang w:bidi='fa-IR'/> affects text shaping but does not configure Word's Table Properties dialog default.

important_decisions.rationale: In compile_gold_standard_chapter4.py lines 80-110 (apply_table_apa7_and_bidi) and lines 309-350 (post_process_openxml), <w:bidi w:val='1'/> was only injected into paragraphs where len(p_text) > 80 or is_heading was true. Because all table cell paragraphs (headers like 'ردیف', 'عنوان فرضیه', numbers like '۰.۲۳۴', p-values like '< ۰.۰۰۱') have len(p_text) <= 80 and are not headings, and because table cell paragraphs are excluded from the body_paragraphs branch, zero table cell paragraphs received <w:bidi w:val='1'/>. When Word inspects a table, seeing that every cell paragraph lacks <w:bidi>, it defaults the table direction in the GUI to Left-to-right.

alternatives_considered.reason: Every paragraph in every table cell must have <w:bidi w:val='1'/> in <w:pPr> to enforce cell-level RTL text flow.
Word requires both table-level bidiVisual and cell paragraph-level bidi to establish consistent RTL orientation.
